A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and all 75 pages, including Appendices A–L. Text, equations, tables, and graphics support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on backdoor removal, refusal-vector transfer, corrupted capabilities, and additional tasks and analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experimental results, including the scalability, humor steering, MediQA, and out-of-distribution evaluations.

M1.justification: The autoencoder and affine mappings, steering procedures, activation replacement, and SAE feature-transfer methods are unchanged, including their appendix descriptions.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same backdoor, corrupted-capabilities, refusal, humor, MediQA, and general-capability datasets and tasks. The appendix evaluations were already present in v3.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same native steering, affine mapping, mean-ablation, random-noise, and weight-patching comparisons. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Model configurations, layer choices, splits, training budgets, metrics, and testing procedures match. Examples include Table 22's three training epochs and 10% validation split, and Appendix I's 20-prompt evaluation.

E4.justification: Layer and magnitude sweeps, noise perturbations, activation and weight patching, SAE feature/probe analyses, and Appendix L's out-of-distribution tests are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 27 retains the same standard-deviation reporting. Appendix H.1 retains averaging over 10 noise samples per prompt and 50 prompts; no uncertainty-reporting or repetition information changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings, and completion examples match throughout. Appendix E still reports 54% mapped versus 56% native steering success, and Appendix I retains approximately 60% mapped humor accuracy.

T1.justification: The mapping equations in Section 3.3, steering formulas in Appendix A, and loss definitions in Appendix D are unchanged. No formal reasoning or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about intervention transfer, corrupted capabilities, cross-architecture transfer, and lightweight safety switches.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning tokenizer differences, brittle backdoors, mapping noise, and limited corrupted-capabilities success are unchanged. Section 8 and Appendix L retain the same applicability limitations and capability-degradation discussion.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, data processing, and evaluation rubrics match across the appendices. Code, dataset, and model access disclosures and their destinations are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to model stitching, activation steering, crosscoders, and other cross-model transfer research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v3, 16 Jun 2025 to v4, 19 Sep 2025. The prose, headings, section order, and appendix organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, legends, and page arrangement are retained throughout. Negligible glyph-rendering differences do not alter the displays or layout.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations are unchanged across the complete PDFs. The updated version/date stamp and negligible typographic differences do not meaningfully affect overall paper quality.
